door.canonical_form: JCS (RFC 8785)-style canonical JSON — Python json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=True)

mapping.note: How the signed card chain lines up with PROV-O, so a provenance-aware agent can read it with a vocabulary it already has. This is a POINTER, not an RDF serialisation — we do not yet emit PROV-O triples.
mapping.prov:Activity: a measurement run over a frozen item bank, identified by bench + task on the axis row
mapping.prov:Agent: did:web:csoai.org — the signing identity, with 5 verification methods in /.well-known/did.json
mapping.prov:Entity: a signed measurement card (public/signed/cards/<sha256>.json) and the public root that includes it
mapping.prov:wasDerivedFrom: card -> the frozen bank items it graded
mapping.prov:wasGeneratedBy: card -> the run that produced it

measurement.lid_note: Quote totals.public_count from the live board. A count typed into a discovery document goes stale the moment the board moves.

notes: CSOAI is NOT a W3C member and is not a participant in any W3C Community Group. This document references PROV-O as a vocabulary we map onto; it claims no affiliation, endorsement, or conformance.

We do not yet emit PROV-O RDF. The mapping above states how our existing structures correspond, so an agent can decide whether our chain is worth reading. When triples are emitted this document will say so.
Anyone can re-check the measurement at /gspc-verify, free, no account.

standard.description: W3C Provenance Ontology — an OWL2 vocabulary for describing how a thing came to be: the entities, the activities that produced them, and the agents responsible.
standard.name: W3C PROV-O
